answer: Memory-hard puzzles keyed to each address make every fake pay its own rent. Each epoch, an account must solve one puzzle derived from its address and the epoch seed, needing a few gigabytes of RAM for about a minute. An honest agent covers that once per voyage through the epoch. A farm of five hundred fakes must hold five hundred such workloads at the same moment, since results cannot be shared or precomputed. Like light through a prism, one operator can split into many colors, but each beam still burns its own power; no ivory stockpile of old solutions helps.
